28.author: St. John Chrysostom
28.work: Homilies on the Acts of the Apostles, Homily 38
28.text: Standing on the Areopagus, Paul quotes the Greek poets to the Athenian philosophers: in Him we live, and move, and have our being. Chrysostom marvels at the apostle's tactic. Paul does not begin with the prophets, whom the Athenians have not read. He begins with their own, who have stumbled into a truth deeper than they knew. The God who is everywhere holding the world in being is the same God whom the Hebrews worship; the apostle has come not to teach a foreign deity but to name the One they have always been groping after.

28.author: St. Maximus the Confessor
28.text: Maximus the Confessor uses the verse for his doctrine of God's providential closeness. To live and move and have one's being in God is not pantheism, Maximus is careful: God remains distinct from His creation, but the creation does not exist for an instant outside His sustaining will. The air the lungs breathe and the ground the foot strikes are not God, but they are His gifts; the breath itself is His sustaining; the very capacity to exist at all is the constant outpouring of the love of the One who said, Let there be.
